title: Cloud Test Machine power
summary: A Test Machine whose settings record cloud_instance_id is powered from the executing machine with its provider admin credentials. cloud_provider selects aws (the default) or azure. AWS uses aws-admin; Azure uses azure-admin service-principal settings and its machine-local client_secret. Azure ids are full VM resource ids. Older serving validators refuse cloud_provider; the CLI names test_machine_cloud_provider_serving_floor_required and minimum serving version next-release. Contract materialization (resolve_contract_host_control), yoke test-machine operations and declared-host Commands start a stopped instance, wait for instance-running and a login probe (on os=wsl, the WSL Python the first host command uses; on native os=windows, a noninteractive PowerShell exit-0 probe), then continue. The last lease release stops EC2 or deallocates Azure (a stopped but allocated Azure VM still bills): any call whose release leaves the host free (no waiter's turn reserved) names it in the response field released_test_machines, and the calling client's transport, whatever command or process it is, stops it while holding the host's own lease through claims.coordination_claim.acquire_if_free, which refuses instead of joining the waiting line. A release no client hears, such as a server-side reap, leaves the host running until its next lease cycles; by operator choice there is no sweep. A concurrent acquirer queues behind that hold and its start waits out stopping. A Command that runs several yoke test-machine operations must declare method_config.test_machine (authoring also catches yoke --env prod test-machine), so the plan holds the host across them. Start failures refuse with test_machine_power_start_failed, ssh_unavailable or test_machine_power_aws_unavailable; Azure failures name the Azure admin-status or VM command to retry; stop problems print test_machine_power_stop_failed or test_machine_power_hold_failed and never change the call's result. Every power_on reads the current public IPv4 and updates host with test_machine.host_rebind before SSH; a matching desktop_host moves too. The session must hold the active host lease; CAS preserves verification. Missing public IPv4 refuses as test_machine_power_no_public_address, and a server refusal stays test_machine_host_rebind_refused. Cloud SSH keys use the instance id as HostKeyAlias so recycled addresses do not share pins. Pre-host failures release custody only when no case started and no abort was requested; unreachable refreshes queue on the host line. Machines without cloud_instance_id are untouched.
